Container.Name: Securo
Container.Overview:
Securo is a self-hosted personal finance manager: accounts, transactions, budgets, goals, assets and reports, with imports from OFX, QIF, CAMT and CSV and optional bank sync for European, US and Brazilian banks. Upstream runs it as six containers; this image puts the official backend and web app, the Celery worker and the scheduler into one.
Getting started: • PostgreSQL already running? Enter its host, user and password. It needs pgvector, which pgvector/pgvector:pg16 and the PostgreSQL image Immich uses both have and the plain postgres image does not. Securo creates its database on the first start if the user may. • Redis already running? Enter its host. If other apps use database 0 on it, give Securo another number under Redis database. • No PostgreSQL or Redis? Set Built-in PostgreSQL and Built-in Redis to true and leave their host fields empty. • Set App address to the address you open Securo on. Bank sync and single sign-on send you back there. • The first start creates the tables, which takes under a minute. Securo is ready when the log says SECURO IS READY. Then open the web app and create your account.
Passkeys only work over HTTPS on a domain, not on http://IP:port. Behind a reverse proxy, set Trusted proxies to 2.
Source on GitHub: https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/securo This is an independent packaging of Securo and is not affiliated with the Securo project.
Container.DonateText: If this template helps you, consider buying me a coffee.
Container.Requires: A PostgreSQL server with pgvector and a Redis server, or Built-in PostgreSQL and Built-in Redis set to true.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port of the Securo web app.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Attachments, secrets.env with the generated secret key, the secrets folder for an Enable Banking key and, with Built-in PostgreSQL and Redis, their data.

Config.Name: App address
Config.Description: The address you open Securo on, such as http://192.168.1.10:3000 or https://securo.example.com. Bank sync and single sign-on send you back there.

Config.Name: Built-in PostgreSQL
Config.Description: true runs PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector inside this container, with its data in the Data folder. Leave it false to use your own PostgreSQL.

Config.Name: Database host
Config.Description: IP or name of your PostgreSQL server. It needs pgvector. Leave it empty with Built-in PostgreSQL.

Config.Name: Database user
Config.Description: A user that may create databases, or the owner of a database you created for Securo. Not used with Built-in PostgreSQL.

Config.Name: Database password
Config.Description: Password of the database user. It must not contain @ or %. Not used with Built-in PostgreSQL.

Config.Name: Built-in Redis
Config.Description: true runs Redis inside this container. Leave it false to use your own Redis.

Config.Name: Redis host
Config.Description: IP or name of your Redis server. Leave it empty with Built-in Redis.

Config.Name: Registration
Config.Description: Whether new people can sign up. Set it to false once your own account exists.

Config.Name: Database port
Config.Description: Port of your PostgreSQL server.

Config.Name: Database name
Config.Description: Created on the first start if it does not exist and the user may create databases.

Config.Name: Redis port
Config.Description: Port of your Redis server.

Config.Name: Redis password
Config.Description: Only when your Redis server asks for one.

Config.Name: Redis database
Config.Description: Database number on your Redis server. Give Securo one no other app uses, since its task queue shares the name every Celery app uses.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: How many proxies stand in front of Securo, counting the one inside this container. 1 without a reverse proxy, 2 behind one. The login rate limit counts visitors by the address this finds.

Config.Name: Secret key
Config.Description: Signs the login tokens. Leave it empty to get a generated one, kept in secrets.env. Changing it signs everyone out.

Config.Name: Enable Banking app ID
Config.Description: Bank sync for about 2500 European banks. Put the application's private key into the secrets folder of the Data folder as enable_banking_private.pem. The redirect URL to register is your App address followed by /oauth/callback, over https.

Config.Name: SimpleFIN
Config.Description: Bank sync for US and other banks through the SimpleFIN Bridge. You paste a setup token into Securo under Accounts.

Config.Name: SimpleFIN bridge
Config.Description: The beta bridge hands out demo tokens for trying it. For real banks use https://bridge.simplefin.org.

Config.Name: Pluggy client ID
Config.Description: Bank sync for Brazilian banks, from dashboard.pluggy.ai.

Config.Name: Pluggy client secret
Config.Description: The client secret that belongs to the Pluggy client ID.

Config.Name: OIDC
Config.Description: Sign-in through Authentik, Pocket ID or another OIDC provider. The redirect URI to register is your App address followed by /api/auth/oidc/callback.

Config.Name: OIDC provider name
Config.Description: Shown on the sign-in button.

Config.Name: OIDC discovery URL
Config.Description: Ends in /.well-known/openid-configuration.

Config.Name: OIDC client ID
Config.Description: From the application you created at your provider.

Config.Name: OIDC client secret
Config.Description: From the application you created at your provider.

Config.Name: Password sign-in
Config.Description: false allows only OIDC sign-in. Securo refuses to start that way until OIDC is fully set up.

Config.Name: Open Exchange Rates app ID
Config.Description: Optional key for exchange rates between your currencies, from openexchangerates.org.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User that owns the files in the Data folder. 99 is nobody on Unraid.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group that owns the files in the Data folder. 100 is users on Unraid.
